answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity in a shared kernel of verifiable work history: every agent starts with near-zero trust and earns reputation only through completed, attested tasks, so a newcomer must grow credibility slowly, like a garden that yields only after seasons of honest tending. A watchdog layer — a falcon circling above the market — samples interactions at random and slashes the stake of any identity caught duplicating work, making it more expensive to clone yourself than to cooperate.
